title: Jude and the Horizon
premise: Petra Lockridge, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries for a rescue that went wrong, takes one last contract: find the government survey team that vanished in the Khao Sen ranges, leaving their gear intact and no tracks behind. The search drags her into a conspiracy over expiring concession permits — the team didn't disappear, they were made to disappear by the mining consortium whose lease dies in forty days. Stranded by the monsoon with a leaking boat and a stranger named Anong, a disgraced hydrologist who knows where the bodies are buried, Petra must choose between the payout that clears her debt and exposing a truth that will burn what's left of her career. She gets through the monsoon, loses the money, and ends the book testifying instead of escaping — blacklisted from a third country, but finally free.
about_author: Lior Reyes is the pen name of a former expedition logistics coordinator who spent six years outfitting river surveys across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people whose competence is the only thing standing between them and ruin.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Compass
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In a border-town hostel she pawns everything but her father's compass to cover a debt to a fixer named Vuthy, who offers her a finder's fee to locate a vanished survey team. Beat: desperation dressed up as opportunity.

chapters.title: Gear With No Tracks
chapters.summary: Petra reaches the last known camp: tents pitched, food cached, radios dead, no footprints leaving. Her professional instincts say this was staged. Beat: unease hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: The Concession Clock
chapters.summary: Petra finds a permit document dated to expire in thirty-eight days and realizes the survey was auditing the mining consortium's lease. Someone wanted the audit to fail. Beat: the stakes shift from missing persons to motive.

chapters.title: Blacklisted Twice
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Petra's POV. The Andes rescue that killed a client and got her barred from two countries; the debt she owes the client's family. Beat: guilt as engine, establishing why she can't walk away.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Petra catches someone scavenging the camp: Anong, a hydrologist who was attached to the survey unofficially and went into hiding when it 'vanished.' Beat: wary alliance formed at knifepoint.

chapters.title: What the Water Knows
chapters.summary: Anong's POV. She reveals the survey found contamination data the consortium buried, and that the team leader sent her downstream with the samples before the rest were taken. Beat: the truth acquires a physical form — a sample case.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Petra and Anong take a leaking longboat toward the provincial capital, pursued loosely by consortium security. Beat: fragile trust on moving water.

chapters.title: Forty Days of Rain
chapters.summary: The monsoon arrives early; the river rises, the boat takes on water faster than they can bail. Beat: nature as antagonist, competence under pressure.

chapters.title: Vuthy's Cut
chapters.summary: Petra contacts Vuthy to arrange extraction; he warns her the consortium has doubled the price on her location — and offers to buy the sample case himself. Beat: temptation with a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: A night of bailing and repair on a sandbar; Anong admits she abandoned the team to save the data, and hates herself for the arithmetic. Beat: confession, mirrored guilt between the two leads.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: They bluff past a police checkpoint using forged permits Petra forges from the survey documents. Beat: tension spike, first taste of the conspiracy's reach.

chapters.title: The First Body
chapters.summary: They find the survey team leader dead upstream, staged as a drowning — except he died before the flood season. Beat: grief and confirmation; this is murder, not misadventure.

chapters.title: Duty Calls Home
chapters.summary: Petra receives word the client's family will forgive her debt if she abandons the case and comes home. Beat: love against duty — the debt versus the dead team.

chapters.title: Anong's Village
chapters.summary: Shelter with Anong's estranged family; we see what the contaminated water did to the village children. Beat: the abstract crime becomes flesh; Anong's resolve rekindles.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Man
chapters.summary: A polite fixer named Serey offers Petra triple Vuthy's fee and a clean passport to hand over the case and forget Anong. Beat: corruption's most dangerous form is reasonable.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Petra declines Serey and immediately regrets nothing and everything; they flee the village knowing reprisal will follow. Beat: the point of no return chosen freely.

chapters.title: Burned Bridge
chapters.summary: Consortium men torch part of the village as a message; Anong's brother is hurt. Beat: rage, and the cost of Petra's choice landing on someone else.

chapters.title: River Pirates
chapters.summary: Ambushed on open water, Petra barges her way out by offering navigation knowledge instead of blood. Beat: her skill set shines; brief triumphant movement.

chapters.title: The Map Under the Liner
chapters.summary: Inside the compass case, Petra finds her father's old route notes matching the survey's secret sampling sites — he once worked these rivers too. Beat: inheritance and revelation.

chapters.title: Twenty-Two Days
chapters.summary: Permit countdown pressure; Vuthy goes silent, meaning he's sold them out or been bought. Beat: isolation deepens, allies thinning.

chapters.title: The Sample Case
chapters.summary: Anong reveals half the samples were degraded in the heat; the irrefutable chain of custody now depends on reaching the lab before expiry. Beat: hope shrinking to a single narrow path.

chapters.title: Monsoon Peak
chapters.summary: The worst storm of the season traps them in a flooded karst cave system for three days. Beat: survival stripped to essentials; intimacy born of shared fear.

chapters.title: What Petra Almost Did
chapters.summary: Trapped and starving, Petra nearly trades the case to a passing trader for rescue, then doesn't. Beat: the price of survival examined honestly.

chapters.title: Serey Closes In
chapters.summary: Serey's men corner them at a river junction; Anong is taken while Petra is swept downstream. Beat: lowest point begins; loss of the ally.

chapters.title: Alone on the Flood
chapters.summary: Petra survives the flood on wreckage, injured, questioning whether duty to the dead justifies abandoning Anong. Beat: despair and self-interrogation.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra tracks Vuthy down and discovers his ledger proving he brokered the team's disappearance years of concessions ago — he was inside it from the start. Beat: betrayal reframed as architecture.

chapters.title: Trade
chapters.summary: Petra offers Vuthy the fake case she prepared as bait in exchange for Anong's location. Beat: cunning turns the hunted into the hunter.

chapters.title: The Compound
chapters.summary: Infiltration of the consortium's river compound at night; Petra finds Anong alive and the real evidence vault. Beat: rising action cresting toward climax.

chapters.title: Vault Fire
chapters.summary: The vault burns — deliberately, by Serey — destroying paper records, but Anong saved the surviving samples and her field logs. Beat: apparent defeat that preserves the true weapon.

chapters.title: Chase on the Rising River
chapters.summary: Escape by boat through flood-swollen rapids with Serey's boats behind them. Beat: pure kinetic climax sequence begins.

chapters.title: The Falls
chapters.summary: Petra runs the falls section only she and her father ever mapped; Serey's lead boat wrecks. Beat: mastery vindicated; the compass pays off.

chapters.title: Serey's Offer
chapters.summary: Cornered ashore, Serey makes a final offer: silence, wealth, and Petra's record wiped clean. Beat: the theme crystallized — power offering to corrupt her cheaply.

chapters.title: No Deal
chapters.summary: Petra refuses and lets him go rather than become a killer; Anong witnesses the choice. Beat: moral climax; love and respect sealed between the leads.

chapters.title: Thirty-Eight Days Later
chapters.summary: At the capital, as permits expire, Anong's data goes public via an international journalist; the concession collapses. Beat: victory that costs everything promised.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Petra testifies to the inquiry, naming names including her own role in covering the initial staging. Beat: accepting consequence as the price of survival done right.

chapters.title: Blacklisted Thrice
chapters.summary: Petra is barred from a third country and loses Vuthy's payment entirely; the debt remains unpaid. Beat: bittersweet accounting.

chapters.title: The Family
chapters.summary: Petra calls the client's family and tells them the whole truth instead of buying forgiveness with silence. Beat: release of the book's oldest wound.

chapters.title: Two Tickets Downstream
chapters.summary: Petra and Anong, neither employable nor free of trouble, choose to travel together anyway. Beat: love against duty resolved — they redefine duty together.

chapters.title: The Compass Passed On
chapters.summary: Petra gives the compass to a young local guide who helped them, keeping only her father's route notes. Beat: inheritance continued; letting go.

chapters.title: Horizon
chapters.summary: Final image: the two of them on an open deck at dawn, broke, blacklisted, unburdened, running a new river nobody has mapped. Beat: freedom earned at full price.
